title: New method turns ocean water into drinking water, without waste
summary: Researchers from University of Rochester have developed a new desalination method that can convert ocean water into drinkable water without producing toxic brine waste. The technique uses a specialized membrane and electric fields to selectively remove ions, making the process more energy-efficient and environmentally friendly than traditional reverse osmosis methods.
problem_solved: This technology addresses the global freshwater scarcity problem by providing a sustainable way to convert seawater into drinking water without the environmental harm caused by toxic brine disposal from conventional desalination plants.
why_valuable: With over 2 billion people lacking access to safe drinking water, this waste-free desalination method could revolutionize water supply in arid regions and coastal cities while eliminating the major environmental concern of brine pollution that affects marine ecosystems.
